name: Netflix Streaming
description: Design a Netflix-like video streaming platform. Covers adaptive bitrate streaming, CDN edge caching, content transcoding, and global content delivery at scale.

learnSteps.title: Adaptive Bitrate Streaming (ABR)
learnSteps.description: Videos are transcoded into multiple bitrate/resolution variants (240p to 4K). The client player measures network bandwidth in real-time and switches between quality levels seamlessly. Content is chunked into 2-4 second segments, each available at every bitrate. The manifest file (DASH/HLS) lists all available variants.

learnSteps.title: CDN Edge Caching & Open Connect
learnSteps.description: Netflix deploys edge servers (Open Connect Appliances) directly inside ISP networks. Popular content is pre-positioned during off-peak hours. With a 95% cache hit rate across 200+ locations, most video bytes never leave the local ISP network. Cache misses fall back to regional or origin S3 storage.

learnSteps.title: Content Pipeline & Metadata
learnSteps.description: The Content Service manages the catalog, recommendations, and playback sessions via the API Gateway. Metadata (titles, thumbnails, subtitles) is cached in Redis with a 92% hit rate. The API path is separate from the video streaming path to optimize each independently.

learnSteps.title: Global Content Delivery Architecture
learnSteps.description: Two data paths: (1) API calls for browse/search/recommendations go through API Gateway to Load Balancer to Content Service. (2) Video streaming goes directly from Client to nearest CDN edge. This separation allows API servers to scale independently from video delivery. Object Storage holds the master copies of all transcoded content.

chaosScenarios.name: Regional Edge PoP Outage
chaosScenarios.description: A regional cluster of CDN edge servers goes dark during evening peak, forcing clients onto farther PoPs and the origin
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Affected clients re-resolve to neighboring PoPs with 30-80ms higher RTT. Video start time degrades and ABR players step down a bitrate tier. Cache hit rate on neighbor PoPs drops as they absorb a cold working set, amplifying origin fetch traffic.
mitigationSteps: Steer traffic away from the failed PoP via DNS/anycast withdrawal
Watch neighbor PoP load — cascading saturation is the real risk, not the dead PoP
Temporarily cap the top bitrate tier in the affected region to cut bytes per stream
Enable origin shield to collapse duplicate cache-fill requests

chaosScenarios.name: Season Premiere Cold-Cache Stampede
chaosScenarios.description: Millions of viewers hit play on a new release simultaneously before edge caches are warm, sending cache-miss traffic to origin storage
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Identical segment requests from 200 PoPs converge on S3. Origin egress spikes 20x; segment fetch latency climbs, players stall on initial buffering. Hit rate recovers within minutes as segments populate edge caches.
mitigationSteps: Pre-position premiere content to all edge locations during off-peak hours before release
Request coalescing at each PoP so one origin fetch serves all concurrent waiters per segment
Stagger regional release times if origin headroom is insufficient
Serve lower-bitrate ladder rungs first while higher tiers warm

chaosScenarios.name: Metadata Cache Cluster Failure
chaosScenarios.description: The Redis metadata cache fails completely, sending all browse, search, and playback-manifest lookups to PostgreSQL
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Database read QPS rises ~12x (92% hit rate lost). Home screen and title detail latency climbs from 30ms to 300ms+. Connection pool saturation begins rejecting queries. In-progress video streams are unaffected — only new browse/play actions degrade.
mitigationSteps: Fail over to the Redis replica; verify replication was current
Enable per-instance request coalescing in the Content Service to deduplicate identical DB queries
Warm the cache with the trending/home-row working set first — it covers most traffic
Serve a static fallback home row from CDN if DB saturation persists

bottleneckProgression.description: Cache-miss browse queries exhaust the metadata DB connection pool as API traffic doubles
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Add read replicas, front with a connection pooler, and raise the cache TTL on stable catalog data

bottleneckProgression.description: Content Service instances saturate on personalization and manifest assembly
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Scale instances horizontally; precompute home-row recommendations per cohort instead of per request

bottleneckProgression.description: API Gateway saturates on TLS termination and JWT validation at peak browse hours
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Scale gateway fleet and cache JWT validation results for token lifetime

bottleneckProgression.description: Origin egress saturates when edge hit rate dips during simultaneous regional cache-fill events
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Raise edge cache retention for the long tail, add an origin shield tier, and replicate origin to a second region

expectedIssues.title: Long-Tail Content Cache Misses
expectedIssues.description: The 5% of requests for unpopular catalog titles miss edge caches, adding 50-100ms segment latency and paying origin egress on every view
expectedIssues.mitigation: Accept it — pinning the full catalog at every edge costs more than the misses; tier rarely-watched titles to regional mid-tier caches

expectedIssues.title: Diurnal Peak Concentration
expectedIssues.description: 70% of daily playback starts land in a 4-hour evening window, so capacity must be provisioned for ~3x the daily average and sits idle overnight
expectedIssues.mitigation: Schedule-based pre-scaling ahead of the predictable peak; use overnight idle for content pre-positioning and batch work

expectedIssues.title: Single-Region Origin Storage
expectedIssues.description: All 200 edge locations fill from one S3 region; a regional storage outage halts cache fill globally and long-tail content becomes unplayable as edge TTLs expire
expectedIssues.mitigation: Cross-region origin replication with automatic edge failover to the secondary origin

expectedIssues.title: Stale Catalog Metadata
expectedIssues.description: With a 1-hour cache TTL, titles removed for licensing reasons can still appear in browse rows, producing playback errors when selected
expectedIssues.mitigation: Event-driven cache invalidation for catalog removals; TTL remains the safety net, not the primary mechanism

steps: Confirm scope from per-PoP health checks — distinguish PoP failure from ISP routing issues
Withdraw the PoP from DNS/anycast steering
Monitor neighbor PoP utilization and origin egress for cascade pressure
Cap top bitrate tier in the region if neighbors approach saturation
Restore and re-warm the PoP before returning it to rotation
Identify the title/segments driving misses from origin access logs
Enable request coalescing and origin shield if not already active
Throttle cache-fill concurrency per PoP to protect origin
Pre-position the hot title to remaining cold PoPs
Check metadata cache hit rate first — most browse incidents are cache incidents
Verify DB connection pool headroom and replica lag
Scale Content Service if CPU-bound after cache recovery

decisions.title: Separate Video Path from API Path
decisions.context: Video bytes outweigh API bytes by 4-5 orders of magnitude and have completely different scaling, caching, and latency profiles
decisions.decision: Stream video directly from client to CDN edge; route only browse/search/manifest API calls through the gateway and Content Service
consequences: Each path scales and fails independently — an API outage doesn't stop in-progress streams
App servers never proxy video bytes
Two distinct monitoring and capacity models must be maintained

decisions.title: Pre-Positioned Edge Content
decisions.context: Release schedules are known in advance and the popularity distribution is extremely top-heavy
decisions.decision: Push predicted-popular content to edge servers during off-peak windows instead of relying purely on demand-driven caching
consequences: 95% byte hit rate; most video traffic never leaves the local ISP network
Premiere stampedes hit warm caches instead of origin
Requires popularity prediction and consumes edge storage for content that may underperform

decisions.title: Cache-Aside Metadata with 1-Hour TTL
decisions.context: Catalog metadata is read millions of times per hour but changes rarely
decisions.decision: Serve metadata from Redis with TTL-based expiry, falling back to PostgreSQL on miss
consequences: 92% of metadata reads never touch the database
Catalog changes can lag up to an hour without explicit invalidation
Cache loss converts instantly into a database load incident

tradeoffs.dimension: Edge Storage Cost vs Origin Egress
tradeoffs.benefit: Origin egress and inter-region transfer reduced to a trickle; best-possible video start times
tradeoffs.cost: Hundreds of edge servers carrying mostly-duplicate copies of the hot catalog

tradeoffs.benefit: Database sized for 8% of read traffic
tradeoffs.cost: Removed or relicensed titles can surface stale for up to an hour without event-driven invalidation

tradeoffs.choice: Capacity sized for the 4-hour evening peak
tradeoffs.benefit: No QoE degradation during the window when nearly all viewing happens
tradeoffs.cost: Significant idle capacity overnight, partially reclaimed for pre-positioning and batch jobs

alternatives.name: Stream Video Through the App Tier
alternatives.description: Proxy all video bytes through the Content Service for unified auth and logging
alternatives.prosVsCons: Single code path and simple session enforcement, but app servers would need 1000x the network capacity and become a global bottleneck
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Bandwidth economics are disqualifying; signed URLs give per-session auth without proxying bytes

alternatives.name: Peer-to-Peer Assisted Delivery
alternatives.description: Let viewers serve video chunks to nearby peers, WebRTC-style, reducing CDN egress
alternatives.prosVsCons: Dramatic egress savings on hot content, but unpredictable QoE, upstream-bandwidth consumption on customer connections, and DRM complications
alternatives.whyNotChosen: QoE control is the product; delegating delivery to uncontrolled peers undermines it

alternatives.name: Multi-CDN from Day One
alternatives.description: Split traffic across two or more commercial CDNs with real-time performance steering
alternatives.prosVsCons: Vendor leverage and failure independence, but doubles integration surface, complicates pre-positioning, and splits committed-volume discounts
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Single CDN with regional PoP failover meets the availability target; multi-CDN is the planned next step if scale or risk profile changes
